newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Boskalis 1996 profit seen down but future.
newsitem.headline: Boskalis 1996 profit seen down but future.

text.p: Dutch dredger Koninklijke Boskalis Westminster NV is expected to post lower 1996 earnings on Thursday, as a better second half performance is unlikely to compensate for a disappointing first six months, analysts said.
But they added that investors were likely to shrug off last year's disappointment as the focus now was on 1997 and the outlook for the dredging sector seemed bright.

Analysts are forecasting full-year 1996 net from ordinary operations of between 62 million and 72 million guilders, with consensus at 66 million. In 1995 the dredger posted ordinary net profits of 71 million guilders.
"Boskalis had a very poor first half and said in August it was uncertain whether it could match the previous year's earnings," said ING Barings' Paul Verbraeken.
Well-filled order books and improved capacity utilisation would boost second half income from normal operations, taking full-year ordinary net to 63 million guilders, he said.
"1997 looks good," Verbraeken added. "Their order books are in good shape and improved margins will also help."
Sven Smit, construction analyst at Bank Labouchere, agreed.
"Boskalis took a bad hit in the first half, partly due to work it took on in 1995 at aggressively low prices.".
"Second half earnings will rise year-on-year. The firm has a good order portfolio and margins have also picked up reasonably well," said Smit, who sees 1996 ordinary net of 65 million.
"The outlook for 1997 is positive, with the Singapore market coming to life and volumes up elsewhere in Asia," he said.

However, competition from Asian players such as Hyundai and Samsung would remain a factor, as would market uncertainty given that many big projects depended on political decision-making which could be fairly arbitrary, he said.
Suez Nederland's Fernand de Boer said dredging prospects for the next two years were good and he saw better 1997 profits.
"Much more important than the result over 1996 -- where I don't think we can expect much in the way of a windfall -- is what Boskalis has to say about 1997," he said.

De Boer, who rates Boskalis a "Buy", sees full-year net from ordinary operations down at 67 million guilders. But he expects the dredger to hold its dividend steady at 1.10 guilders, based on an improved outlook.
"(Builder) Ballast Nedam has already expressed optimism about dredging trends in the next two years," he said. "It's a sector with a lot of potential."
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
